parsed.study_design: Case study using secondary-data time-series and household-budget analysis
parsed.population_and_sample: Czech households by income decile during 2005–2012, supplemented by aggregate domestic-water data covering approximately 94% of inhabitants connected to public water systems
parsed.exposure: State economic regulation and changes in regulated water and sewerage tariffs, examined alongside household income
parsed.outcome: Household water-and-sewerage expenditure as a percentage of net income, affordability/water poverty, domestic water consumption, and price and income elasticity of demand
parsed.rationale: The Materials and Methods section (pp. 33–35) identifies an empirical analysis of Czech Statistical Office household surveys and national water-service price and consumption series, with tariffs and state regulation as the exposure. The Results and Discussion section (pp. 35–37) reports consumption-price dependence, demand elasticities, and water-and-sewerage affordability by household income decile, including the proportion facing water poverty. These are empirical affordability, quantity, and exclusion-related outcomes for household water and sanitation services.
